title: Video shows half-drunk pint exploding in UK's 'most haunted' pub
excerpt: Video shows an unattended Guinness suddenly shattering with nobody anywhere near it - and no plausible explanation
content:
This is the moment a half-drunk pint exploded spontaneously in a 'haunted' pub without being touched - that staff blame on the ex-landlady's ghost. Footage shows an unattended pint of Guinness sat on the bar at the Farmer's Boy pub in Brickendon, Hertfordshire, suddenly shattering - spilling glass and the Irish stout over the bar.

Landlady Rachel Drury has rubbished sceptics' claims it was caused by thermal shock - a cold drink in a hot glass - as the punter is a regular who would have refused a warm pint.

Instead, Rachel, who's owned the boozer for two-and-a-half years, reckons it's the work of a former landlady from the 19th century making her presence known.

The 52-year-old said this isn't the first time she's experienced her spirit lingering in the pub, claiming the kindly spook once patted her back when she was 'really' stressed.

Rachel shared CCTV footage online of the glass shattering on July 20, with the caption: "Our pub is apparently one of the most haunted in the UK?? What do you think happened here?"

The spooky clip racked up more than 200,000 views, with both sceptics and believers flooding the post with their thoughts. The mum-of-three said psychics believe the pub is home to a number of ghosts including the former landlady and her child, who are 'friendly'.

Rachel, from Brickendon, Hertfordshire, said: "I live upstairs. Someone told me about it and I checked the CCTV. It was one of my regular customers who always drinks Guinness and he left it on the bar while he went to the loo. And then that happened.

"It just collapsed. The guy whose pint it was drinks Guinness all the time and if it had been poured in a hot glass, he would have refused it. There are a lot of comments about glasses breaking if they are too hot and you pour cold drinks in it.

"It can't have been a warm glass, if there was a scientific reason it would have happened earlier. The person whose pint it was is convinced it must be (a spooky explanation). He knows the pint glass was perfect."

Nonchalant Rachel said it's not the first time the friendly ghost has made her presence known. She said: "I'm not scared, I've never once felt unsafe. The number of people who have been to the pub or have worked for me that have seen and felt things is huge.

"A number of my staff who do believe in the paranormal are convinced that they've seen a woman. When they are closing up and there is no one else in the pub, they are convinced that they turn around and someone is standing there.

"Whoever it is that is here just wants to be nice, it always feels warm and welcoming. Customers have felt something has brushed past them or one leg has felt hot as if someone is touching their leg.

"There was one night I went to bed and my husband was in the living room, I was really stressed at the time. I lay in bed and I could feel someone patting me on the back, I got up and nobody was there. It was quite a nice feeling.

"The pub is from the 1800s. When I've spoken to people born here, we think that it's potentially an old landlady. When we've had psychics come in, they've said they are kind spirits, there is no horribleness. We believe it is a woman and a child."

People flooded the posts with comments about what was behind the mystery explosion.

One wrote: "Must be an Irish ghost." Another commented: "It could be one of the old locals and you're in his seat."

One added: "Get the vicar in to bless the place, can't be having pints wasted." Another commented: "That's not paranormal it's to do with temp it's probably just been cleaned and not cooled."
